Consistency of Road Geometry in DTP-OSM
Ensure that the geometry of all Priority roads* in DTP-OSM is consistent with the current OSM dataset.

And the OSM dataset as a reference
When the geometry of each DTP-OSM road segment is compared to OSM
Then at least 98% of Priority road* segments must have geometries consistent with OSM
And consistent geometry is defined as segment vertices representing roads will be within 0.01m of the OSM feature geometry.
*Note: Additional nodes created from segmentation should be excluded from this analysis.
column11: JJ: This is aligned to the intent of MM current state. Need to clarify how DTP want to segment the network, as there is breakdown of OSM ways to align to VicMap segments built into the DTP OSM Network. What if an OSM way does not break at an intersection?
column12:
The only way I can see this metric being calculated is via node coordinate comparison between DTP and OSM networks. If 98% of nodes coordinates from OSM are present in DTP (within 0.01 m) then this would be met. However, I do not see how this metric is possible if comparing DTP features to OSM features, since DTP features are commonly different to OSM due to VicMap features alignment differences.
I'm also unsure where in the process they intend this to go, i.e., is it a whole-network analysis after each update, or only on the features which have been updated in that changeset? Or is this an entirely separate process to running updates, kind of like a data quality review process.

column12: This would be an extension onto the existing MM process. I suspect it is due to DTP wanting to be able to update, review, and submit to LRS changes in a specific region with the intent of not needing to consider changes made outside that region. I suspect most of the effort here would be in frontend, but the backend would also need to either introduce new step function processes to run in this case, or modify the existing step function, or (the better option) to rework the archicture to support these alternative paths better (e.g., a more general API not hardcoded step function processes). This would also require the functionality added to allow DTP to manually trigger updates which is not something that currenlty exists, it shouldn't be too hard, but we'd need to consider possible ramifications from this.
